did_you_know.text: Did you know? Samuel reminded Saul that his kingship came from the LORD’s calling: he had been anointed king over Israel, and therefore he was required to listen to the LORD’s words and obey them.
Did you know? Saul assembled 200,000 infantrymen for the campaign, along with 10,000 men from Judah.
Did you know? Before the battle, Saul warned the Kenites to distance themselves from the Amalekites because they had shown kindness to the Israelites when they came out of Egypt.
Did you know? Saul captured Agag, king of the Amalekites, alive, even though the command was to devote everything belonging to Amalek to destruction.
Did you know? Saul and the people spared Agag and the best of the sheep and cattle, but they destroyed the possessions they considered less valuable.
Did you know? After the LORD told Samuel that He regretted making Saul king, Samuel was distressed and cried out to the LORD all night.
Did you know? When Saul met Samuel, he claimed that he had obeyed the LORD’s command. But immediately afterward, Samuel asked him about the sound of the sheep and cattle he heard in the background.
Did you know? Samuel taught that listening to the LORD is better than offering burnt offerings and sacrifices, expressing it in these words: “Behold, to obey is better than sacrifice.”
Did you know? Saul admitted that he had disobeyed the LORD because he was afraid of the people and listened to them, thereby acknowledging his personal responsibility as a leader.
Did you know? When Samuel turned to leave, Saul grabbed the edge of his robe, and it tore. Samuel used the torn robe as a symbol that the LORD had torn the kingship away from Saul.
